title: NY State Senate · District 30
area: Central and northern Manhattan: Harlem, East Harlem, Morningside Heights, Hamilton Heights, Washington Heights, and parts of the Upper West Side.

context.text: Both the Democratic and Working Families Party primaries scheduled for June 23, 2026 were canceled; incumbent Cordell Cleare advanced on both lines without appearing on a primary ballot. The Republican primary was also canceled and, as of this writing, no Republican or other opposition candidate has filed for the general election, leaving Cleare unopposed on the ballot.

candidates.name: Cordell Cleare
candidates.ballotNote: Unopposed; no Republican or third-party opponent has filed for the general election.
candidates.currentRole: New York State Senator, District 30 (since November 2021)

summary.text: Cordell Cleare is the Democratic and Working Families Party nominee for re-election to New York State Senate District 30, which covers Harlem, East Harlem, and adjoining Manhattan neighborhoods. A Harlem native, she was a tenant organizer, school board leader and longtime chief of staff to State Senator Bill Perkins before winning a 2021 special election to the seat. She chairs the Senate Aging Committee and is unopposed in 2026.

background.text: Raised in Harlem, where, according to her official biography, her family has lived for four generations; attended New York City public schools, including Brooklyn Technical High School.

Worked as a tenant organizer and chaired the New York City Coalition to End Lead Poisoning, whose work her official biography credits with shaping the city's Childhood Lead Poisoning Prevention Act (Local Law 1 of 2004).
Served as Board President of Community School District 3 (Upper West Side and Central Harlem) and then as President of its Community Education Council.
Served as chief of staff to Bill Perkins during his service on the New York City Council and in the State Senate, starting in 1997.

Served as a Democratic District Leader representing parts of East and Central Harlem, co-founded the Michelle Obama Democratic Club, and, per her official biography, was among the first Democratic Party officials in New York State to support Barack Obama's 2008 presidential campaign.
Ran in the June 2021 Democratic primary for New York City Council, placing fourth of 14 candidates, according to her official biography.

Won the Democratic nomination through the County Committee and then a November 2, 2021 special election for the State Senate seat vacated when Brian Benjamin was appointed Lieutenant Governor, with about 89% of the vote (88.6% per Ballotpedia); took office November 30, 2021 and was re-elected in 2022 and 2024.
Chairs the Senate Aging Committee and sits on committees including Education, Housing, Construction and Community Development, Social Services, and Investigations and Government Operations.

According to her official biography, during the COVID-19 pandemic she ran a food pantry operation, distributed personal protective equipment, and registered voters; the biography lists her as a 2026 Women of Distinction honoree and a 2026 New York State Senate Veterans' Hall of Fame honoree.

priorities.text: Reparations and economic, environmental, restorative and racial justice.
"Truly affordable housing" and housing safety in her district.
Quality schools and equitable education, including accountability for charter schools.
Access to healthy foods for district residents.
Ending gun violence and domestic violence, and supporting workforce development and job creation.

record.text: Sponsored S10548, the Citizens Utility Board Act, which would create a board funded by voluntary consumer dues to represent residential utility ratepayers before the Public Service Commission, with a $1 million state appropriation for startup; in Senate Finance Committee as of May 20, 2026.

Sponsored S10578, extending brownfield redevelopment tax credits for a stalled project at 1800 Park Avenue in East Harlem; in Senate Investigations and Government Operations Committee as of May 26, 2026.

Sponsored S10341, establishing the Harlem Unified Community Planning urban renewal agency to enable community-driven local economic development planning; referred to the Senate Local Government Committee as of May 14, 2026.

Chairs the Senate Aging Committee in the 2025–2026 session and also sits on the Cities 1, Education, Corporations Authorities and Commissions, Housing, Investigations and Government Operations, and Social Services committees.
